Thus the Apostle rightly warned long ago: Take care that no one falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and through it many be defiled, Heb. 12:15. Those are in great danger who, together with the Pharisees, Jews and all the Justiciaries, seek purity of life while neglecting true sanctification, without which, the Apostle said (v. 14), no one shall see God. This sanctification does not consist in any righteousness and holiness at all, but in true sanctification [ἁγιασμῷ], that is, in true righteousness and its fruit, liberty and charity, arising from faith that is not feigned, 1 Tim. 1:5. Those who neglect it are in such a state that they take pleasure in their own righteousness, in the outward works that shine before men, in abstaining from certain blameworthy sins, and in the wonderful obedience of rites, and from these they expect life and salvation, from which there follows an increase of death and eternal damnation. You are severed from Christ, all you who are justified by the law; you have fallen from grace, Gal. 5:4. This is that root of bitterness springing up and troubling everything, Heb. 12:15, and also the root bearing poison and wormwood [שרש פרה ולענה], Deut. 29:18–19. History shows that this is the case among those who favour Judaizers, Cathari, Pelagians, Novatians, Donatists, and above all Antichrist, who, with true knowledge of Christ and true righteousness buried, promise themselves salvation from their own works.

units.la: XL. Pharisæorum & Gnosimachorum genuinus fœtus est fatalis ille Monachatus, qui Ecclesiæ & populo Christiano mature satis oneri esse cœpit, religionis vim paularim reso vit, & faciem ejus plane decolorem reddidit. Is primum à piis hominibus, in Ægypto præcipuè, ob persecutionum diritatem urbes relinquere, & deserta loca inhabitare compulsis, suscepta, abstinentiæ, devotionis, humilitatis, & domandæ carnis non usitatum antea modum docuit. Cujusmodi instituta, quandiu intra ἐχωπαςμὸν, seu liberam observantiam, & innocua pietatis adminicula & exercitia constiterunt, laudem potius quàm reprehensionem meruerunt. Ast ubi authores eorum nimiis encomiis celebrari, & plures eorum instituta æmulari coeperunt, novarum inventionum nec finis nec modus fuit; ex quibus etiam regulæ & canones formati sunt, ad quorum amussim quisque sub specie pietatis, vitam componeret. Inde Eremi pertœsi, iu urbes penetrarunt, & in iisdem fixam immobilemque sedem collocarunt. Cumque in iis Monachorum nomen & omen, nisi certo vitæ instituto, vestitu, habitu, domicilio à cæteris civibus separati implere non possent, paulatim Monachatus Pharisaicus ejusmodi invectus est, qui indies incrementis majoribus augescens, tandem, in tot species distractus est, ut tot jam in Papatu religionum novarum facies visantur, quot Monachorum ordines & examina glisceunt. Et, quod pudendum in primis est, eò illi dementiæ processerunt, ut & Ordinem Ignorantiæ instituerint, vulgato eriam adagio, nihil Monacho tndoctus esse; & cæca obedientia, jurati in verba non Dei, sed homimivis superioris, qui & ipse non Deo, sed Papæ soli devotus est, voto se omnes adstringant. Neque Monachi soli, sed omnes insuper Papæ clientes cæca fidei, quam carbonariam dicunt, idolo litantes, notitiam fundamenti verbi Dei, & eorum, quæ eidem superstrui debent, fidei adimunt, adeóque fidei in Christum oculum effodiunt. Nam & Bellarmini piacularis illa vox est, fidem melius per ignorantiam, quàm per scientiam definiri. Et juxta plerosque illos nihil scire, tutissima vita est. Cúmque Papæ ipse, cui sacramento omnes Papicolæ dicunt, & cujus religiosis dictatibus aures substringere omnes tenentur, omni salutari notitia rerum Divinarum destituatur, & verbum Dei in se permanens non habeat, dubitari non potest, quin Papatus Gnosimachorum hæresi & impietate infectus totus sit.
units.tr: XL. That fatal monasticism is the genuine offspring of the Pharisees and the enemies of knowledge. It soon became a burden to the Church and the Christian people, gradually weakened the power of religion, and made its face quite colourless. At first it was taught by pious men, chiefly in Egypt, who were driven by the savagery of persecutions to leave the cities and dwell in deserted places, and it introduced a practice of abstinence, devotion, humility and the taming of the flesh of a kind not used before. While such institutions remained within free observance [ἐχωπαςμὸν], that is, within free discipline, as harmless aids and exercises of piety, they deserved praise rather than blame. But when their founders began to be celebrated with excessive eulogies, and many began to imitate their institutions, there was no end or limit to new inventions, from which rules and canons were also formed, by whose measure each man, under the appearance of piety, would order his life. Hence men weary of the desert penetrated into the cities and settled there in a fixed and immovable seat. And since, among them, they could not fill the name and mark of monks unless they were set apart from other citizens by a particular manner of life, dress, habit and dwelling, a Pharisaic monasticism of this kind gradually was introduced, which, growing daily by greater increments, at last was split into so many kinds that there are now as many new faces of religion visible in Popery as there are orders and sects of monks that spring up. And, what is most shameful, they went so far in madness that they even established an Order of Ignorance, and, with the common saying, nothing is more untaught than a monk, all bind themselves by a blind obedience, sworn to the words not of God but of a human superior, who himself is devoted not to God but to the Pope alone. Not only the monks, but all the clients of the Pope, offering sacrifice to the idol of a blind faith, which they call charcoal-burner's faith, take away from faith the knowledge of the foundation of the Word of God and of what ought to be built upon it, and so they put out the eye of faith in Christ. For that is the unhappy saying of Bellarmine, faith is better defined by ignorance than by knowledge. And according to most of them, to know nothing is the safest life. Since the Pope himself, to whom all Papists say they are sworn, and whose religious decrees all are bound to obey, is destitute of all saving knowledge of divine things, and does not have the Word of God abiding in him, there can be no doubt that the whole of Popery is infected with the heresy and impiety of the enemies of knowledge.

units.tr: XLI.

units.la: Tametsi infaustus & adulter ille Pharisaismi & Gnosimachorum partus, cujus γνῶσις character est, salutis per opera & fictam sanctimoniam affectata consecutio, ab omnibus fere sectis, ab Evangelica Ecclesia si discesseris, pro legitima prole adoptatus, & intimum in contubernium admissus est; præ cæteris tamen omnibus Socinianis, & eorum similis, Remonstrantibus placuit. Socinianti enim quicquid in religione μυστηριώδες est, & humanæ rationis conditionem investigari & penetrari nequit, illud omne tanquam ἀλόγον proscribere pridem ausi sunt. Unde incarnatio λόγος, satisfactio propeccatis, & quicquid olim Judæis offendiculum posuit, atque gentilibus stultitia fuit, & hodieque τοῖς ἔξω omnibus est, id omne una litura inducere & abolere iis placuit, quasi nulla inter homines pax, nisi abolito unico pacis remedio, quod Christus θεάνθρωπος, & mortis ejus pretium atque valor est, coalescere; nec Christiani, nisi negato prius, vel saltem inutili facto Christo, nuncupari possent. Illam porro religionem optimam esse illi decernunt, quæ omnibus hominibus maximè accommodata & placita est, quámque omnes, vel plerique homines cum sensu suo conciliare possunt. Planè enim religionem quam invexerunt, Theologiæ naturalis perfectior quidam typus est, cujus perfectionis author Christus cùm sit, ab illo Christianam religionem denominant. Cujus summam in eo constituunt, ut quis præcepta & promissa Christi aprimè cognita habeat; sic tamen, ut promissa exquisitè investigari non debeant, dummodo summam eorum vitam æternam esse constet, & præcepta rectè intelligantur. Ut jam cardo religionis Socinianæ in observantia mandatorum Dei sub spe
units.tr: Although that unhappy and adulterous offspring of Pharisaism and the Gnosimachi, whose mark is knowledge [γνῶσις], that is, the eager pursuit of salvation through works and feigned holiness, has been adopted as legitimate offspring and admitted to intimate fellowship by almost all sects, if you exclude the Evangelical Church, it has pleased the Socinians and their like, the Remonstrants, above all others. For the Socinians have long dared to reject as irrational [ἀλόγον] everything in religion that is mysterious [μυστηριώδες] and cannot be investigated or grasped by the condition of human reason. Hence they have agreed to wipe out and abolish, in one stroke, the incarnation of the Word [λόγος], satisfaction for sins, and whatever once was a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles, and is still foolishness to those outside [τοῖς ἔξω]. As if there could be no peace among men unless the one remedy of peace were abolished, namely Christ, God-man [θεάνθρωπος], whose death is the price and value of peace; and as if no one could be called a Christian unless Christ were first denied, or at least made useless. They further decree that the best religion is that which is most suited and pleasing to all men, and which all men, or most men, can reconcile with their own sense. For the religion they have brought in is clearly a more perfect sort of natural theology, and since Christ is its author, they call it Christian religion. They place its sum in this: that a person should have a thorough knowledge of Christ's precepts and promises; yet the promises need not be investigated closely, provided it is agreed that their sum is eternal life and the precepts are rightly understood. Thus the hinge of the Socinian religion turns on the observance of God's commands in hope

units.la: Socinianis genuini Gnosimachi sunt, quia & ex Theologia Ethicam cudunt. alterius vitæ vertatur. Atque id cùm homini etiam citra revelationem constare possit, manifestum est, religionem illorum non esse nisi Ethicam nomine Christi incrustatam. Hinc Socinus epist. 11. ad Dudith. profitetur, sufficere ad cognoscendum iter, quod ad salutem Cœlorum perducit, ut sciamus, quæ revera præcipiantur, vel vetentur à Deo, adeo ut si in reliquis error occurrat, nemo ob eum Cœlo excludi debeat. Idem de fide & operibus p. 136. id solum ad salutem nequiri sciscit, ut pie vivamus, & mundanis cupiditatibus valedicamus; supervacaneum esse judicans, cogitare de his, quæ Christi personam attinent, una cum iis omnibus, quæ Christus pro nobis fecit & facturus est, quatenus per ea justificari velimus.
units.tr: For the Socinians are genuine Gnosimachi, because they also forge ethics out of theology. of the other life turns. And since this can be known by man even without revelation, it is plain that their religion is nothing but ethics dressed up in the name of Christ. Hence Socinus, in Epistle 11 to Dudith, declares that it is enough for knowing the way that leads to the salvation of heaven that we know what God truly commands or forbids, so that if error occurs in other matters, no one should on that account be shut out of heaven. Likewise, in On Faith and Works, p. 136, he holds that for salvation it is enough only to live piously and bid farewell to worldly desires, judging it superfluous to think about those things which concern the person of Christ, together with all the things that Christ has done and will do for us, insofar as we wish to be justified by them.

units.la: XLII. Iidem Socinians articulos fidei alios fundamentales, alios non fundamentales faciunt.
units.tr: XLII. The same Socinians make some articles of faith fundamental and others not fundamental.

units.la: Cæterum nec in genere satis definiunt, quinam articuli fundamentales sint; nec in specie eos recensent, sed satis habent fundamentales minuere, & ex utrorumque numero doctrinam de Trinitate, æterna Filii generatione, Spiritus S. hypostasi, peccato originali, perfectione legis, persona Christi θεάν‑θρώπῳ, ejusque satisfactione pro nobis, aliosque summovere. Tum articulos fidei metiuntur non ex tota doctrina Christiana, sed altera duntaxat ejus parte, lege scilicet, ad cujus duo capita, fiduciam & obedientiam, eosdem reducunt. Denique fidei veritate & sinceritate in Christo posthabita, ad solam pietatem cuncta referunt, & Theologiam universam ita mere practicam faciunt, ut totam fidei doctrinam, quæ ex verbo Dei ab orthodoxis traditur, ceu inutilem, & speculationibus otiosis duntaxat inservientem explodant, eo quòd sive credita, sive non credita, parum ad fiduciam & obedientiam Deo Christóque debitam, utpote quæ sola & unicè necessaria sint, faciant.
units.tr: Moreover, they do not define sufficiently in general which articles are fundamental, nor do they list them in particular; but they are content to diminish the fundamentals and, from the number of both kinds, to remove the doctrine of the Trinity, the eternal generation of the Son, the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, original sin, the perfection of the law, the person of Christ, the God-man [θεάνθρωπος], and his satisfaction for us, and others. Then they measure the articles of faith not by the whole of Christian doctrine but only by one part of it, namely the law, to whose two heads, trust and obedience, they reduce them. Finally, with the truth and sincerity of faith in Christ set aside, they refer everything to piety alone, and make theology so purely practical that they cast off the whole body of doctrine that the orthodox derive from the Word of God as useless and serving only idle speculations, because, whether believed or not believed, it makes little difference to the trust and obedience owed to God and Christ, which alone are necessary and absolutely required.

units.la: XLIII. Socinianorum vestigia uti in aliis, ita hic etiam graviter Remonstrantes legunt.
units.tr: XLIII. As the Socinians' footsteps are found in other matters, so here too the Remonstrants read them closely.

units.la: Illi enim nullum doctrinæ vel fidei articulum, prout ab operibus distinguitur, fundamentalem & præcisè ad salutem necessarium ducunt, nisi forte unicum hunc, quòd accessuri ad Deum credere debeant, Deum esse. Qualis fides etiam in Diabolis reperitur, neminemque adeò, nisi aliud accedat, salvare potest. Atqui necessitatem cognitionis Christi, & fidei in eundem, Curcellæus, Remonstrantium eorum, qui τὸ χάριν... proficiunt (2 Tim. III. 13.) coryphæus, Differt. III. de Necessit. Cognit. Christi ad salutem, Cel. Maresio opposita, aperto Marte oppugnare ausus est. Proin juxta illos in unica doctrina operum totius rei cardo vertitur. De caeteris enim doctrinae capitibus absque praejudicio veritatis & salutis disputare, quadrata, quod ajunt, rotundis mutare, de iis aliter, atque veritas postulat, judicare, & in solidum etiam illa ignorare, fas tutúmque ducunt. Disciplinam quinetiam Ecclesiasticam non ad doctrinae, sed ad vitae duntaxat, & morum emendationem extendunt. Neque alia ratio est, ob quam haereticorum & haeresium patrocinium suscipientes, palam defendunt, Regnum Christi consistere posse, etiamsi omnes ejus subditi ab haereticis seducerentur; & haeresin non peccatum, sed meram, summamque simplicitatem esse, ipsos denique haereticos ob solam probitatem aeternum beari posse. Ne quid de prophetandi, quam tantopere urgent, libertate dicam, quam in eo ponunt, quod quisque sequi & probare, quod cum Spiritus S. mente congruere putat: atque juxta judicium suum, toto licet Coelo à judicio Dei disparatum, Deum colere, cum certa spe salutis, possit. Denique eodem tendit illorum dogma de salute gentilium probè viventium, licet Evangelium prorsus ignorent. Quos, si certa eorum salus est, non per id, quod credunt, sed quod faciunt, salutem consequi necesse est. Quae cuncta Gnosimachorum haeresin de novo paxillo suspendere, & penitus incrustare, meridiano jubare clarius est.
units.tr: For they do not regard any article of doctrine or faith, as distinct from works, as fundamental and strictly necessary for salvation, except perhaps this one alone: that whoever comes to God must believe that God exists. Such faith is found even in the devils, and cannot save anyone unless something else is added. Yet Curcellaeus, the leader of those Remonstrants who make progress for the worse [προκόψουσιν ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον] (2 Tim. III. 13.), in his Third Dissertation on the Necessity of Knowing Christ for Salvation, opposed to the famous Maresius, has dared to attack the necessity of knowing and believing in Christ with open war. Therefore, according to them, the hinge of the whole matter turns on the single doctrine of works. For they think it lawful and safe to dispute about the other heads of doctrine without prejudice to truth and salvation, to change square for round, as the saying goes, to judge of them otherwise than truth requires, and even to be wholly ignorant of them. Nor do they extend church discipline to doctrine, but only to the correction of life and morals. And there is no other reason why, by taking up the patronage of heretics and heresies, they openly defend that the kingdom of Christ can stand even if all its subjects are led astray by heretics; that heresy is not a sin but pure and supreme simplicity; and that heretics themselves can be blessed eternally on account of their uprightness alone. I say nothing of the liberty of prophesying, which they press so hard, by which each may follow and approve whatever he thinks agrees with the mind of the Holy Spirit, and may worship God with a certain hope of salvation according to his own judgment, though it be wholly at odds with the judgment of God in heaven. Finally, their dogma about the salvation of Gentiles who live uprightly, even though they are utterly ignorant of the Gospel, tends to the same end. If their salvation is certain, it must follow not from what they believe but from what they do. It is clearer than midday that all these things hang up the heresy of the Gnosimachi on a new peg and fix it firmly in place.

units.la: XLIV. Atque haec de Gnosticis & Gnosimachis, & utrorumque partibus, quas in Ecclesia ad haec usque tempora traxerunt, dicta sufficiant.
units.tr: XLIV. Let these remarks on the Gnostics and Gnosimachi, and on the parties of each that they have drawn into the Church down to the present time, suffice.

units.la: Ex quibus illud abunde constat, errores non intra principium suum consistere, sed aquarum profundarum instar (Prov. XVIII. 4.) altos plerunque habere fundos, & juxta verissimum illud S. Pauli, βεβήλους κενοφωνίας profanas sonorum vanitates ad ulteriorem semper impietatem proficere, denique sermonem eorum, ut gangraenam, serpere, 2. Tim. II. 16. 17. Tum & illud liquidò inde cognoscitur, quàm plena periculi res sit, mysteria pietatis à pietate divellere, & vel ex sola notitia rerum Divinarum, vel ex sola vitae puritate affectata salutem aeternam sibi aliisque promittere. Quorum utrumque haeresin, omni tempore in Ecclesia Dei profligatam, spirat; & spirat jure meritóque, uti ex sequente diatriba, qua utriusque necessitatem inevitabilem, & sororium atque indissolubile vinculum ex Dei verbo demonstrare, σὺν θεῷ καὶ παλάμῃ conabimur, manifestum evadet.
units.tr: From these things it is abundantly clear that errors do not remain within their origin, but, like deep waters (Prov. 18:4), usually have deep bottoms; and, according to that most true saying of St Paul, profane babblings [βεβήλους κενοφωνίας], that is, profane vanities of sound, always advance to greater impiety, and finally their word spreads like a gangrene (2 Tim. 2:16–17). It is also plainly learned from this how perilous a thing it is to tear the mysteries of godliness away from godliness, and to promise eternal salvation to oneself and others either from the bare knowledge of divine things or from a merely pretended purity of life. Each of these heresies, though put down in the Church of God at every time, breathes on, and rightly and deservedly so, as will become manifest from the following discourse, in which we shall attempt, with God's help and effort [σὺν θεῷ καὶ παλάμῃ], to show from the word of God the unavoidable necessity of both, and their sisterly and indissoluble bond.

units.la: DEO SOLI SAPIENTI ET SANCTO GLORIA.
units.tr: TO GOD ALONE, THE WISE AND HOLY, BE GLORY.

units.la: F I N I S.
units.tr: THE END.
